pr_title: oidc authenticator: make library usage easier
pr_body:
oidc authenticator: allow passing in CA via bytes

This change updates the OIDC authenticator code to use a subset of
the dynamiccertificates.CAContentProvider interface to provide the
root CA bytes.  This removes the hard dependency on a file based CA
and makes it easier to use this code as a library.

Signed-off-by: Monis Khan <mok@vmware.com>

---

oidc authenticator: allow specifying a KeySet directly

This change updates the oidc authenticator to allow specifying an
oidc.KeySet as an input option.  This makes it possible to
synchronously initialize the KeySet instead of relying on the
asynchronous initialization that is normally done to support
self-hosted providers.  This makes it easier to use this code as a
library.

Signed-off-by: Monis Khan <mok@vmware.com>

---

issue_context.title: OpenID Connect token authenticator cannot be (easily) used in a controller
issue_context.body:
#### What would you like to be added:

Allow for controllers to easily consume the [oidc authenticator](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/be99f37a6861f885c263a447656b9470ba4f720f/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/plugin/pkg/authenticator/token/oidc/oidc.go), by allowing it to have the OIDC issuer CA bundle passed as `[]byte` and offering a way to construct the `Authorizer` without any async polling. This should not result in any end-user facing change.

#### Why is this needed:

In a [webhook authenticator](https://github.com/gardener/oidc-webhook-authenticator) that tries to dynamically add new OpenID Authenticators by calling `New(opts)` https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2f263b24a7aab78c794fb90339c176678de6bf8e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/plugin/pkg/authenticator/token/oidc/oidc.go#L217

the following problems are faced:

- there is no indication, if the authenticator has been successfully initialized as it runs in a goroutine - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2f263b24a7aab78c794fb90339c176678de6bf8e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/plugin/pkg/authenticator/token/oidc/oidc.go#L221-L231 - ideally, if there is a network issue when requesting the JWKS, your controller would get the error from OIDC provider initialization and handle it (put it in a rate-limited queue).
- The certificate authority of the OIDC issuer can only be a file on the filesystem, requiring the developer to [create a temp file with the CA data](https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/pinniped/blob/0a7c5b06047a7ae526c5476d1c7329b353cf700a/internal/controller/authenticator/jwtcachefiller/jwtcachefiller.go#L156-L169) and use it for creating such OIDC authenticators. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2f263b24a7aab78c794fb90339c176678de6bf8e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/plugin/pkg/authenticator/token/oidc/oidc.go#L81-L82

/sig auth

review_comments: Does this actually reload? It seems like we take the first and pass it to the transport.

Right, this does not reload today.  There are two `TODO(enj)` in this PR that would need to be addressed to make CA reloading work.  I left those out since I would have to wire up a context through the authn stack to prevent go routine leaks and would need some custom logic in the OIDC authn code to update the root CA when it changed.
Do we care that the removal of this field may cause compile failures for downstream consumers of this package?
No, these repos offer no [compatibility](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/README.md#compatibility) across versions.
Do we care to dynamically reload the `KeySet` like we do in the `else` block? This might be helpful for someone who wants to provide an out-of-band rotating set of keys dynamically.
`KeySet` is an interface, not a struct.  Users are free to rotate the keys as they see fit.  This is what the default `remoteKeySet` does automatically via the `jwks_uri` data.
